text:
Anna R: quick idea for Private onboarding: ephemeral 'claim' tokens that avoid long-lived peering. thinking of a single-use claim flow to issue short-lived tenant certs. want early feedback.
Mike L: high-level? how is this better than peering + console provisioning?
Anna R: main differences: 1) no VPC attachment needed for initial bootstrap, 2) claim = single-use signed blob tied to agent pubkey, 3) control plane issues short-lived cert + route assertion, 4) agent opens outbound authenticated connection within TTL.
Julio P: how do we prevent replay or stolen claims?
Anna R: bind claim to agent_pubkey_fingerprint and claim_nonce; claim transitions: CREATED -> CONSUMED -> ACTIVE. require outbound mTLS probe from agent within window. one-time-use only.
SRE Bot: ops notes: rate-limit claims per-account, per-IP. emit metrics: claims_created, claims_consumed, claims_failed, claim_revokes.
Sarah K: product: UX must be "Create claim" -> CLI runs -> success. need audit fields (created_by, consumed_by_ip, consumed_at). TTLs for renewals and enterprise team-claims mode.
Mike L: fallback for accounts without PrivateLink?
Anna R: fallback to regional relay origin; we should model relay capacity for different onboarding RPS.
Julio P: what about Dedicated customers who want ENI/peering later?
Anna R: plan: ephemeral claim for bootstrapping, optionally follow up with provisioning flow that creates per-tenant ENIs or peering for stable throughput.
Mike L: failure recovery: add revoke endpoint and GC if agent never finishes attaching downstream endpoints. edge rejects expired route assertions.
Anna R: next steps: I'll run a small cost/latency spike for 3 onboarding scales and draft an RFC. Julio will help threat model; Mike looks at GC windows.
Sarah K: sounds good, please include audit UI and admin revoke in RFC.
SRE Bot: created INFRA-1345 for relay estimation.
